economics.government-analyse-1.0005.all: Plan: profit motive -> cost cutting -> job losses, lower wages/conditions (why unions oppose); rising passengers -> expansion, new jobs, training; less job security.

economics.government-analyse-2.0004.all: Plan: state can hold fares down (prices above inflation); run for public service not profit -> better service; reinvest; long-term planning; strategic transport network.

economics.government-assess-1.0002.all: Plan: efficiency, investment for rising passengers, better facilities vs monopoly charges, loss of subsidised safety spending; depends on regulation/competition; judgement.

economics.government-assess-2.0001.all: Plan: for - high prices, poor service, natural monopoly, essential good; against - cost of buying, taxpayer losses, state inefficiency; regulation alternative; judgement.

economics.government-define1.0002.all: Transfer of ownership of a firm/industry from the private sector to the public sector (state).

economics.government-define2.0006.all: A market where one firm can supply the whole market at a lower average cost than two or more firms could (1), due to huge fixed costs / economies of scale, e.g. water pipes (1).

economics.government-describe.0008.all: To protect a strategic industry (1) such as rail/energy vital to the economy or national security (1); or to save jobs if the firm would collapse.

economics.government-evaluate-1.0006.all: Plan: as assess-1 with sustained judgement on short vs long run and role of regulator.

economics.government-evaluate-2.0002.all: Plan: as assess-2 for rail; judgement on whether regulation achieves the same at lower cost.

economics.government-explain.0002.all: Port owner seeks profit (1) so may raise port charges, which are passed on in higher prices (1); without Istrova's subsidies, safety/facility spending may fall, worsening service (1).

economics.growth-analyse-1.0006.all: Plan: new factories/mines -> jobs, lower unemployment; higher incomes/living standards; more tax revenue for public services; profits -> investment.

economics.growth-analyse-2.0005.all: Plan: lower consumer spending -> lower revenue/profit; cut output, investment, staff; closures; energy costs squeeze margins; inferior-good firms may gain.

economics.growth-analyse-3.0002.all: Plan: education -> skills, productivity; infrastructure -> lower costs, attracts FDI; productive capacity rises -> LRAS right -> real GDP up.

economics.growth-assess-1.0004.all: Plan: jobs, incomes, tax vs pollution externality, inequality, resource depletion, inflation; depends on sustainability/distribution; judgement.

economics.growth-assess-2.0004.all: Plan: falling AD -> lower demand-pull inflation; but energy prices -> cost-push persists; depends on length of recession/policy; judgement.

economics.growth-assess-3.0003.all: Plan: low income N€4,000 -> growth reduces poverty; but opportunity cost, time lag, conflicts with inflation/environment/inequality; judgement.

economics.growth-define1.0006.all: The pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time around the trend rate of growth.

economics.growth-define2.0008.all: The level of material well-being of people (1), measured e.g. by real GDP per capita (1).

economics.growth-describe.0013.all: Falling real GDP (1) for two consecutive quarters (1); or rising unemployment as firms cut output.

economics.growth-data.0011.b: Plan: falling spending -> lower revenue, profit; cut output/investment/jobs.
economics.growth-data.0011.c: Plan: lower demand-pull vs energy cost-push; depends on duration/policy; judgement.
